name: Love and Money
techniques: full-bleed flat colour hero panel with a single oversized wordmark
off-white second panel with a torn/pixel-edge black mask dividing hero from work grid
small square case-study thumbnails pinned to a light grid background
palette: hard red (studio's own LAM red) against solid black in the hero, switching to an off-white ground with black type for the work section
type: huge tight-tracked black slab/grotesk caps for the wordmark, small caps tagline set dead centre under it
motion: the page reads as two static colour blocks in sequence rather than a scroll animation, letting the red-to-white cut do the pacing
why: two colours and one oversized wordmark carry the whole homepage - there is no hero image to hide behind

name: Emi Takahashi
techniques: dense right-rail information table (clients, collaborators, education) run alongside every project image, catalog-style
bilingual Japanese/English labelling used as a design element, not a language switcher
large documentary-style nature photography paired with small archival ephemera thumbnails
palette: warm paper-white ground, muted green and moss tones from the nature photography carrying the colour instead of any brand accent
type: small, dense sans-serif set in a strict multi-column table grid, kanji and Latin type given equal visual weight
motion: static, list-driven; the craft is in the information architecture (a running resume/CV interleaved with imagery) rather than in transitions
why: treating a portfolio as an annotated archive - every image ships with its own metadata table - reads as considered rather than as a gallery of pretty pictures

name: Gil Huybrecht
techniques: an award/recognition list (Awwwards SOTD, FWA, Webby, Lovie) set as plain text sidebar rather than badges
tight uniform grid of small square project thumbnails, no captions until hover
flat black ground with no imagery in the hero at all
palette: pure black ground, white text, no accent colour - the thumbnails supply all the colour
type: small utilitarian sans for the credentials list, same weight used for name and for nav
motion: no visible hero animation; the page leans entirely on grid density and restraint
why: listing awards as a plain inline text line instead of a trophy shelf keeps the page from turning into self-promotion

name: Artem Taradash
techniques: mixed serif-in-sans headline treatment ("Everything around us is love" in serif, "Design is how it takes shape" in sans) inside one sentence
case-study teaser cards mixing product photography (an electric delivery van) with a smartwatch UI close-up
circular rotating signature/logo mark used as a nav element
palette: warm cream ground with black text, product photography (grey van, dark watch face) supplying cool contrast
type: serif/sans pairing used mid-sentence for emphasis rather than for hierarchy between sections
motion: not evaluated beyond the static render; layout is card-based scroll
why: switching typeface mid-headline to carry meaning (poetic clause in serif, functional clause in sans) is a small, specific move worth stealing for a single strong sentence

name: Nick Clement
techniques: client logo strip (BBC, PlayStation, Checkout.com) set directly under the value proposition instead of at page bottom
warm editorial product photography used as a full-width proof panel between case studies
a liquid/ink-blot colour reveal that resolves into a client wordmark (numan) as a case-study opener
palette: near-black ground with white type, one warm terracotta/orange photograph breaking the monochrome, a violet ink-blot accent on the numan case study
type: clean geometric sans, small size for the eyebrow role, larger weight-matched size for the one-line pitch
motion: the ink-blot resolving into a logotype is the one deliberate transition; everything else is a static case-study stack
why: putting recognisable client logos immediately below the headline, at small size and low contrast, sells credibility without turning the hero into a badge wall

name: Atlason
techniques: the nav labels (Works / More) are set at the same oversized size as the wordmark, functioning as both navigation and headline
an asymmetric photo grid of furniture/interiors sits directly beside the type instead of below it
a full-height studio portrait anchors the left column while the grid scrolls independently on the right
palette: warm off-white/cream ground, near-black condensed type, terracotta and walnut tones from the product photography
type: big, tight, condensed grotesk caps used for wordmark and nav alike - no visual demotion between the two
motion: static grid; the type-as-navigation idea is the craft move, not the animation
why: collapsing the nav bar and the H1 into a single row of equally-sized words is a genuinely different information hierarchy than a small nav plus a big hero headline

name: Klikkentheke
techniques: catalog-style numbered project rows (accession numbers like 1420-1431) instead of titled case studies
muted desaturated thumbnail treatment inside an otherwise near-white layout
small serif nav label against a plain grey ground, archive-reading-room tone throughout
palette: pale warm grey ground, near-black text, muted desaturated imagery with no accent colour
type: small serif for structural labels (catalog, numbers), functional sans for everything else - a librarian's type system, not a marketing one
motion: not evaluated beyond the static render
why: numbering work like archive accessions instead of naming it as "projects" reframes a studio site as a research collection

name: Grafik
techniques: bilingual Māori/English headline set stacked in the hero, both languages given full-size treatment rather than one as a subtitle
bold flat-orange condensed display type laid directly over a high-contrast portrait photograph
a floating pill-shaped edit/menu control in the corner used as the only chrome
palette: black ground, one saturated orange-red accent carrying all the display type, full-colour portrait photography for contrast
type: heavy condensed grotesk caps, tightly leaded across three centred lines
motion: not evaluated beyond the static render
why: giving the Māori-language line equal size and placement to the English line, rather than treating it as a footnote, is a genuine content decision that shapes the whole hero

name: Isaac Leon
techniques: a wordmark treated with a trademark glyph ("Isaac León TM") as a small piece of self-aware branding
a one-line credit list of collaborators set directly under the name instead of on a separate about page
small uniform thumbnails for wildly different project types (UI, motion, product) held to one grid so the range reads as one practice
palette: plain white ground, black type, thumbnails supplying the only colour
type: large serif-adjacent display wordmark against small utilitarian sans body copy - one clear size jump, nothing in between
motion: not evaluated beyond the static render
why: the TM mark after a personal name is a tiny, specific piece of tone-setting that a generic "Hi, I'm ..." headline would not achieve

name: Viktor Horvath - Enroute
techniques: a single lowercase wordmark filling nearly the full viewport height as the entire above-the-fold content
a vertical colour-block band (a tall "B" panel) used as a graphic divider rather than a photograph
typeface credited by name (FK Grotesk) directly in the case study rather than left to guesswork
palette: near-black ground, white type, one flat red vertical band as the sole accent
type: an oblique/expanded grotesk (FK Grotesk) set at a scale where the wordmark alone defines the page's proportions
motion: not evaluated beyond the static render
why: crediting the exact typeface in the case study is the kind of specific, checkable detail that turns a portfolio piece into a usable reference for someone else's project

name: Casa Gay 1893
techniques: a heritage date (1893) set as an oversized numeral directly under the wordmark, doing the trust-building work a badge or paragraph usually does
warm tablescape product photography paired with a founding-history paragraph on the same first screen
a muted navy-and-burgundy palette held across both hero and product photography rather than switching to white for commerce
palette: deep navy/burgundy ground with warm terracotta and brass tones from the tableware photography, no bright white anywhere above the fold
type: ornate serif numerals for the date, a plain serif wordmark, Spanish-language body copy in a smaller companion serif
motion: not evaluated beyond the static render
why: keeping a dark, warm palette through the commerce sections instead of dropping to a white product-grid template is what makes the 1893 heritage claim feel considered rather than decorative

name: Whole Earth Index
techniques: a plain-text mission statement as the entire hero, no imagery, no button
a grid of magazine-masthead wordmarks (Whole Earth Catalog, CoEvolution Quarterly, Soft-Tech) used as the primary navigation into the archive
scanned cover thumbnails with visible wear, left unretouched, dated by season and year
palette: flat black ground, white and off-white type, the scanned magazine covers supplying the only colour and texture
type: a condensed slab/serif for each masthead reproduction, plain monospace-leaning sans for the descriptive text
motion: static archive browsing, no transitions to evaluate
why: using the actual historical mastheads as clickable navigation, instead of a generic 'Browse the archive' button, makes the typography of the 1970s source material do the wayfinding

name: Paul Kalkbrenner
techniques: a strict column-ruled grid overlaid on a huge display headline, with solid black circular bullets marking word breaks between grid columns
a small square artist photo inlaid mid-word inside the wordmark itself
a streaming-service icon row (Apple Music, Amazon Music, Deezer, iTunes, Beatport) set at uniform small size as the sole footer-style CTA
palette: stark white ground, solid black type and grid rules, a small greyscale photograph for the only tonal variation
type: very large tight grotesk caps broken across a five-column numbered grid (01-05), read as a layout system rather than a single headline
motion: not evaluated beyond the static render
why: printing the grid's own column rules and numbers visibly, instead of hiding them, turns a plain typographic hero into a diagram of its own construction

name: CcType
techniques: the specimen word ("Timeline") repeated at ascending point sizes down the page, largest at the bottom, so scale itself becomes the layout
a dark specimen panel with each word given its own grey background block, isolating letterforms for comparison
plain top nav (Fonts / Pairs / Licenses / Trials / Buy) kept identical across every typeface's page
palette: light warm-grey specimen ground giving way to a near-black panel lower on the page - the type is the only colour event
type: the product is the typography: a grotesk/slab specimen typeface (CcTimeline) shown at a dozen sizes on one screen with no other content competing for attention
motion: not evaluated beyond the static render
why: letting a type specimen page be nothing but scaling instances of one word is the correct amount of restraint for a foundry selling craft, not marketing

name: Mowellens
techniques: a scrolling marquee of plain-text benefit claims ("native agriculture", "paraben free", "zero artificial flavors") run above the fold instead of icons
amber apothecary-glass product photography lit against a warm neutral backdrop
an email-capture modal that repeats the hero's own headline rather than introducing new copy
palette: warm cream and amber ground, deep brown glass bottles supplying the accent colour, no cool tones anywhere on the page
type: plain serif for the wordmark, small tracked-out sans caps for the claim marquee
motion: not evaluated beyond the static render
why: running product claims as a plain scrolling text ticker, styled like a stock ticker rather than a badge row, is a specific, low-cost way to pack in proof points without cluttering the hero

name: Mogutable
techniques: a flat-lay hero of small ceramic and dried-ingredient objects scattered on a plain ground, used in place of a lifestyle photograph
a lower-case dotted wordmark (mogutable.) as the entire brand mark
a white product grid with price tags set directly under each square photo, no hover reveal needed
palette: warm neutral flat-lay ground (sage, terracotta, bone) in the hero, switching to plain white for the commerce grid
type: small lower-case serif wordmark with a trailing period, plain sans for product names and prices
motion: not evaluated beyond the static render
why: a flat-lay of the actual small objects sold, arranged as an editorial still life rather than a banner ad, sets the tone before any product grid appears

name: Sliders
techniques: a farewell letter ("Tak for 12 fantastiske ar") set as long-form centred body copy on a plain black ground, used for a restaurant's closing announcement rather than a menu
a gold script logotype as the sole graphic element above the letter
moody, warm burger-and-fries photography reserved for the very end of the page, after the text
palette: solid black ground, warm gold script accent, saturated amber and red tones in the closing photograph
type: a gold hand-drawn script for the logotype against small, centred serif body copy - a wedding-invitation register for a burger restaurant
motion: not evaluated beyond the static render
why: using a plain long-form letter, not a photo montage, to close out a 12-year-old restaurant brand treats the announcement as writing rather than as marketing

name: Soilboy
techniques: a bonsai photographed against a pale blush ground as the entire hero image, no supporting copy beyond a four-word claim
a lower-case wordmark set in a plain grotesk, kept small relative to the product photo
a plain three-column plant grid with prices in the local currency (SGD) set directly under each pot
palette: soft blush-pink and warm stone ground, deep green foliage supplying the only saturated colour
type: small lower-case grotesk wordmark and nav, letting the plant photography carry the visual weight instead of display type
motion: not evaluated beyond the static render
why: cropping the hero photo tight on a single bonsai's silhouette, rather than a shelf of products, makes a plant shop feel like a considered object rather than inventory

name: HPI Real Estate
techniques: a three-word vertical stack headline ("Service. Integrity. Results.") set over a full-bleed warehouse photograph
a rotating featured-developments card with a plain numbered counter (03/05) instead of visible dot pagination
animated stat counters (portfolio size, client count) that read as zero at first paint
palette: navy-blue overlay on daylight industrial-building photography, white type, a single blue CTA button as the only saturated accent
type: bold condensed sans stacked in three short declarative lines, small labels under each stat counter
motion: the numbered counter card implies an auto-advancing carousel behind a static featured-developments panel
why: three one-word sentences stacked as the entire headline is a plainer, more confident move than the usual real-estate paragraph of reassurance copy

name: Andluca
techniques: a row of flat geometric window-pane illustrations used as the hero graphic for a literal smart-window product
a two-button audience switch (Homeowners / Industry partners) set directly under the headline instead of in the nav
a labelled technical diagram of the product's glass layers placed immediately after the hero, before any lifestyle imagery
palette: pale sky-blue ground with white cloud illustration, matched to the literal product category (windows/sky)
type: plain geometric sans for the headline ("Powered. Wireless. Intelligent."), small caps eyebrow label above it
motion: not evaluated beyond the static render
why: illustrating the hero with the product's own literal form (window panes against sky) rather than a generic tech-gradient graphic keeps a hard-to-photograph product legible at a glance

name: Fontshare
techniques: a live specimen size slider (up to 120px) with an editable sample-text field, letting the visitor type their own word into the specimen
a filter toolbar (categories, properties, license) styled like a font-manager application rather than a marketing page
list-view and grid-view toggles for browsing the catalogue
palette: near-black specimen panels for dark-mode browsing, switching to plain white for the catalogue grid, no other brand colour
type: the product is the type: each row renders its own typeface (Satoshi, Clash Display) at full specimen size, editable live
motion: not evaluated beyond the static render
why: making the specimen text editable in place, instead of a fixed pangram, is the one feature that actually helps someone choose a typeface for their own project

name: ETQ Amsterdam
techniques: monochrome studio product photography (grey knitwear against a grey ground) so garment and background nearly merge
a plain lower-case wordmark set as tracked-out small caps rather than a logo mark
short declarative product copy ("Worn daily. Built to last.") set beside, not under, the photograph
palette: muted grey-on-grey palette across both photography and ground, no saturated accent colour visible above the fold
type: small tracked sans caps throughout, no display-size headline - the photography carries the scale instead of the type
motion: not evaluated beyond the static render
why: letting the garment and the backdrop sit at nearly the same grey value is a deliberate low-contrast choice that reads as quiet confidence rather than a lighting mistake

name: Scope Copenhagen
techniques: a two-line contradiction headline ("What we do might seem simple. But only at first glance.") used as the entire hero, no image behind it
interior photography cropped into small paired thumbnails rather than one full-bleed shot
a plain text link ("Projects") used as the only call to action, styled identically to body copy apart from the underline
palette: plain white ground, black type, warm neutral interior photography (linen, walnut) as the only colour
type: large tracked sans caps for the two-line headline, the same weight used for both sentences despite their contradictory meanings
motion: not evaluated beyond the static render
why: a headline that argues with itself in two flat, same-weight sentences does more to signal a considered design studio than a portfolio grid would on its own

name: Matt D'Avella
techniques: a press-mention logo row (Wired, Business Insider, Today) placed directly under the newsletter signup form rather than in a footer
a warm, editorial (not stock) portrait photo used as the entire hero background
testimonial cards with small round avatar photos run in a single-row strip, no carousel arrows visible
palette: warm cream ground, a large lifestyle portrait supplying muted denim and skin tones, no bright brand colour
type: bold rounded sans for the headline ("Don't sacrifice your soul to the algorithm"), small sans for testimonials and press logos
motion: not evaluated beyond the static render
why: leading with a contrarian, slightly confrontational headline about the algorithm - not with subscriber-count bragging - is the specific copy choice that keeps a creator's newsletter page from reading as generic

name: Charbono
techniques: full-bleed black-and-white archival-style photography (a wide-brimmed hat, vineyard workers) as the entire hero, with the wordmark simply overlaid, no gradient scrim
long-form heritage prose (the 1976 Judgment of Paris) set in a narrow right-hand column beside the photograph rather than below it
an italic script wordmark used as the single colour-free accent over monochrome imagery
palette: pure black-and-white photography throughout the hero and history sections, no colour introduced until (presumably) product shots further down
type: an elegant italic serif logotype (Charbono) set small and centred over the photograph, plain serif body copy for the history text
motion: not evaluated beyond the static render
why: committing to black-and-white photography through the entire heritage section, instead of colour-grading it warm, makes a wine brand's history read as documentary rather than as lifestyle marketing

name: Good Books
techniques: a soft, out-of-focus colour-gradient blob used as the only hero graphic behind a plain headline
a Warren Buffett pull-quote set in large serif type with specific words underlined by hand rather than bolded
a row of small circular avatar photos (Mr Beast, Ann Miura-Ko, Ray Dalio) used to introduce "featured people" instead of book covers
palette: pale off-white ground, a soft blurred pink-to-blue gradient as the sole colour event, black text throughout
type: large serif for the pull-quote with selective underlines standing in for emphasis, small sans for the interface chrome (nav, avatar labels)
motion: not evaluated beyond the static render
why: underlining specific words in a pull-quote by hand, rather than styling the whole quote in italics, mimics an annotated book page and fits a reading-recommendation product

name: MemberFirst Mortgage
techniques: a four-tile "I'm looking to..." intent picker (purchase, refinance, build, partner) used as the hero instead of a single generic CTA
a two-column benefits grid (turn-times, rates, fit, service) with a plain line-icon per tile
warm residential photography reserved for the intent-picker thumbnails rather than the main banner
palette: corporate navy-blue ground with white cards, warm homeowner photography breaking up the blue in small doses
type: plain corporate sans throughout, no display headline larger than the intent-picker labels
motion: not evaluated beyond the static render
why: routing every visitor through a four-way intent picker immediately, instead of one generic "Get Started" button, is a specific way to shorten a mortgage site's decision path

name: Zenit
techniques: a headline built from cropped word-fragments ("...ility.", "...gration.", "...ndardisation.") that only resolve once the viewport is wide enough, implying scale before it is legible
a steep upward architectural photograph (looking up through a lattice tower) used as the hero image
a plain cookie-consent panel left visibly unstyled against the branded page around it
palette: black-and-white architectural photography, near-black ground, no colour accent above the fold
type: large bold sans caps, deliberately cropped at the viewport edge so only word endings are legible in the render
motion: not evaluated beyond the static render
why: cropping headline words at the frame edge so only their endings show is either a deliberate scale device or a responsive bug - either way it is a specific, checkable detail for a build review

name: The Maker Makes
techniques: a two-photo hero pairing (a garden bed and a close leaf shot) run side by side for a single recipe post, rather than one wide banner
plain category tags (Gardening, Seafood, Asian-inspired) set directly under each post title in the featured grid
a small line-drawn avocado icon used as a scroll-cue at the base of the hero instead of an arrow
palette: plain white ground, garden greens and food photography supplying all the colour, black text throughout
type: plain serif for post titles, small sans caps for category tags and metadata
motion: not evaluated beyond the static render
why: a hand-drawn avocado standing in for the generic down-arrow scroll cue is a tiny, specific brand touch that costs nothing but is easy to skip

name: Pure Cosmetics
techniques: a product-in-hand photograph (a lip gloss with a built-in light and mirror) used to demonstrate the actual product feature rather than describe it in copy
a discount claim (SAVE 20%) set as oversized red type directly inside the hero rather than as a top banner
a swatch-style four-product row with strike-through/sale pricing shown inline
palette: deep magenta/black ground in the hero, switching to plain white for the product grid, hot-pink packaging supplying the accent
type: bold condensed sans for promotional claims, plain sans for product names and prices
motion: not evaluated beyond the static render
why: photographing the lip gloss's built-in light actually turned on, in someone's hand, demonstrates the feature the product name promises instead of just naming it
